event_name: Saturday Adventures at the Center: Book Spotlight “Sofia Valdez, Future Prez”
event_description: Continue celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month with a special Storytime at the Center. During this engaging program, Center staff will read Sofia Valdez, Future Prez, the inspiring story of a young girl who learns that when something needs to change, anyone can step up and make a difference. Through Sofia’s journey, children will explore themes of leadership, perseverance, civic engagement, and using their voices to help their communities. Following the reading, families can participate in a hands-on activity designed to encourage creativity and problem-solving while reinforcing the story’s message that every person, no matter their age, has the power to create positive change. Perfect for young learners and their caregivers, this interactive experience helps children see themselves as future leaders and changemakers. Readings take place at 12pm and 1pm   Are you a local author with a story to share? Submit an inquiry to be considered for a Saturday Adventures Storytime and inspire the next generation of readers, thinkers, and changemakers.

event_name: A Worthy Objective: National Teachers Day at the Center
event_description: In honor of National Teachers Day, the Center invites educators to enjoy an afternoon of inspiration, exploration, and appreciation. Inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s belief that education should provide both “the power of concentration” and “worthy objectives on which to concentrate,” this special event offers teachers the opportunity to experience the Center at their own pace while discovering exhibitions, programs, and resources designed to support learning beyond the classroom. Throughout the afternoon, the Education Team will spotlight resources available to teachers through facilitated Field Guide experiences and Traveling Trunk demonstrations, providing ideas for bringing civil and human rights education into classrooms and learning spaces. Educators can also participate in art and history activities that celebrate the curiosity and creativity at the heart of great teaching. Whether you’re looking for classroom inspiration, educational tools, or simply an afternoon to explore, we invite you to celebrate the power of education at the Center.

event_name: Saturday Adventures at the Center
event_description: Join us this Saturday for an unforgettable experience with interactive storyteller Mama Koku, who will lead high-energy, improvised storytelling sessions at 12 p.m. Known for her magnetic stage presence, Mama Koku transforms storytelling into “story-doing,” inviting children and families to step into the narrative and become part of the performance. Each session is lively, creative, and completely unique, blending imagination, movement, and collaboration in a way that keeps audiences fully engaged. While you’re here, be sure to explore Change Agent Adventure: Children’s Gallery, an interactive space designed for children 12 and under. This hands-on “secret headquarters” invites kids to play, create, and build confidence as they discover what it means to be a changemaker. About the Storyteller Mama Koku is a celebrated teaching artist and storyteller known throughout Metro Atlanta for her dynamic and interactive style. A graduate with honors from North Carolina Central University, she studied theater with concentrations in performance and education. She began her career as a high school theatre teacher, where she honed her work as a storyteller and children’s writer. Her engaging approach has earned her recognition as the Official Teller for the National Black Arts Festival’s Education Village and The Coretta Scott King Book Awards Book Fair. Website: Mama Koku | Watch the Stories Come to Life

event_name: Saturday Adventures at the Center: Storytime with Joanne Telcide-Bryant
event_description: Join author Joanne Telcide-Bryant, Ed.S. for a special Storytime in the Change Agent Adventure gallery as she shares her engaging holiday-themed children’s book. Through this heartwarming story, young readers will celebrate the joy of the season while building vocabulary, literacy skills, and reading comprehension through a story filled with gratitude, family traditions, and festive cheer. Perfect for children and families, this interactive Storytime offers a unique opportunity to hear directly from the author while exploring themes of thankfulness, kindness, and community. After the reading, guests will have the chance to engage with the book’s literacy-focused activities, including discussion questions designed to strengthen reading comprehension and encourage a deeper connection to the story. With more than 1,200 literacy words, a glossary, and interactive learning elements, this special event combines the magic of storytelling with the power of education and imagination. Learn more about Joanne and her team at her website: Foster Critical Thinking for Children with Josh & Nelly’s Books Are you a local author with a story to share? Submit an inquiry to be considered for a Saturday Adventures Storytime and inspire the next generation of readers, thinkers, and changemakers.

event_name: CIVICS 4 ALL AGES!!
event_description: The fight for justice, equality, and civic participation belongs to all of us, and it is never too early to begin learning how to make a difference. CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! is a special family learning experience that helps participants better understand how government works, why civic engagement matters, and how individuals can create change in their communities. Through engaging discussions and real-world examples, families will explore the foundations of civics in a welcoming and accessible environment. Hosted in the Action Lab and Rotunda, the program is designed for both adults and young learners, with activities tailored to each audience. The experience begins with youth-focused programming that introduces civic concepts through interactive, kid-friendly activities before shifting to sessions designed for adults, allowing every family member to participate and learn. Whether you’re looking to build your civic knowledge, spark meaningful family conversations, or inspire the next generation of changemakers, CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! offers a unique opportunity for the whole family to learn, engage, and grow together.

event_name: National Buy Nothing Day at the Center
event_description: The day after Thanksgiving is often known as one of the biggest shopping days of the year, but National Buy Nothing Day invites us to pause and think differently about consumption, community, and the impact of our choices. Join the Center for an afternoon of learning and reflection as we explore how everyday purchasing decisions affect people, communities, and the environment. Through engaging activities and conversations, visitors will gain new perspectives on ethical consumption and discover ways to make more intentional choices. In partnership with the Atlanta Tool Bank, guests can participate in special “My Passion” sessions to learn about each organization’s mission and how they help build a more sustainable Atlanta. The event will also feature an ethical footprint-themed art activity, a live artist painting experience, and a donation collection that encourages giving back to the community. Whether you’re interested in reducing waste, rethinking consumer habits, or finding practical ways to make a positive impact, National Buy Nothing Day at the Center offers an inspiring opportunity to explore sustainability, stewardship, and community action.

event_name: Saturday Adventures at the Center: Book Spotlight “Peaceful Fights for Equal Rights”
event_description: Join us for a meaningful Saturday Storytime featuring Peaceful Fights for Equal Rights. In recognition of Human Rights Month, families are invited to gather for an engaging reading that introduces young learners to the people and movements that have worked to create a more just and equitable world. Through thoughtful storytelling, children will discover how peaceful action, courage, and perseverance can inspire positive change. Following the story, guests can participate in a hands-on activity inspired by the book’s themes. Designed for children and families, this interactive experience encourages reflection, creativity, and conversation while exploring the values of fairness, empathy, and standing up for others. Readings take place at 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. in the children’s gallery. Are you a local author with a story to share? Submit an inquiry to be considered for a Saturday Adventures Storytime and inspire the next generation of readers, thinkers, and changemakers.
